                     About this report
                     The 2025 Annual Report outlines the strategic priorities and key developments
                     that shaped Adyen over the past year. It gives readers a clear view of our
                     business, financial performance, and risk management, while offering deeper
                     insight into the topics that guide our operations and support Adyen’s long-term
                     growth.
                     The year in review summarizes key milestones of the year. Adyen at a glance
                     gives a high-level overview of who we are and what we do as a company. In the
                     rest of the Management Review we discuss our approach to key focus areas in
                     our business, showing the steps we have taken this year to support our long-term
                     success. Following this, the Corporate Governance chapter outlines the
                     structures and policies that ensure effective oversight, transparency, and
                     accountability within our organization.
                     This year marks the second year of our Sustainability Statement, which sets out
                     our material sustainability topics and the way these are identified, managed, and
                     reported in accordance with the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive
                     (CSRD) and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). Together,
                     the Management Review,the Corporate Governance chapter and the
                     Sustainability Statement constitute the Management Report. Finally, the
                     Financial Statements provide a comprehensive account of Adyen’s financial
                     position, performance, and cash flows over the reporting period.
                     To support navigation, readers can move between sections of the report using the
                     buttons at the bottom of each page. These provide direct access to each chapter
                     and allow for intuitive browsing throughout the document.

                                                                                                                               Message from the
                                                                                                                               Co-CEOs
                                                                                                                               Dear reader,
                                                                                                                               We are proud of the progress we made in 2025 as we continued executing
                                                                                                                               against our long-term vision. Our focus remained consistent throughout the year:
                                                                                                                               building a financial technology platform that enables our customers to operate
                                                                                                                               with greater efficiency, resilience, and control as they scale globally.
                                                                                                                               Macroeconomic and geopolitical developments in the first half reshaped the
                                                                                                                               operating environment for some of our customers, prompting them to reassess
                                                                                                                               where and how they grow. Policy shifts, including changes to U.S. tariffs,
                                                                                                                               accelerated the need to pivot to new regions. We supported our customers
                                                                                                                               through these changes by enabling them to enter and scale in alternative markets
                                                                                                                               with speed and confidence. Using our single platform and licensed infrastructure,
                                                                                                                               they could access local payment rails and maintain consistent performance
                                                                                                                               without reworking their setup.
                                                                                                                               As AI continued to be a central topic within the financial services industry, our
                                                                                                                               customers were highly engaged in understanding its potential impact on their
                                                                                                                               businesses. Our approach remains grounded: we build with our customers in mind
                                                                                                                               and we apply AI where it meaningfully improves outcomes. By embedding
                                                                                                                               intelligence directly into our infrastructure, rather than treating it as a standalone
                                                                                                                               capability, we strengthen how payments, risk, and financial flows operate end
                                                                                                                               to end.
                                                                                                                               The scale of our data, combined with our single tech stack and AI, is enabling a
                                                                                                                               new level of performance across the platform. This is evident in the evolution of
                                                                                                                               Dynamic Identification as a foundational layer. Built on our single stack and
                                                                                                                               banking infrastructure, it draws on trillions of interactions across online and in-
                                                                                                                               store commerce to inform decisions in real time. As fraud grows more
                                                                                                                               sophisticated, Dynamic Identification allows us to move beyond static checks and
                                                                                                                               instead balance security, conversion, and customer experience with greater
                                                                                                                               precision — supporting safe, scalable commerce.

                                                                                                                               Adyen at a glance
                                                                                                                               Adyen is the financial technology platform trusted by the world’s leading
                                                                                                                               businesses. We simplify global commerce by replacing what is traditionally a
                                                                                                                               fragmented, multi-party setup with a single platform built entirely in-house.
                                                                                                                               Our product offering spans both payments and financial services, all operated end-
                                                                                                                               to-end on our own infrastructure and banking licenses. This model gives us a level
                                                                                                                               of control, reliability, and global consistency that sets us apart. It enables us to
                                                                                                                               support enterprise and platform customers with complex, worldwide operations.
                                                                                                                               Our approach is pragmatic and customer-centric. We continuously evolve our
                                                                                                                               platform and offerings to address long-term customer needs. We build products
                                                                                                                               that work seamlessly across regions and benefit all customers rather than a single
                                                                                                                               use case. This philosophy shapes how we innovate and how we partner with the
                                                                                                                               businesses we serve. With 4,771 FTEs and 29 offices across 21 countries, our
                                                                                                                               teams collaborate directly across time zones, guided by the Adyen Formula —
                                                                                                                               our principles for decision-making that keep us building with speed, autonomy,
                                                                                                                               and the long-term top of mind.
                                                                                                                               We organize our commercial activities into three pillars. Digital supports online-
                                                                                                                               first enterprises such as subscription businesses, travel, and mobility. Unified
                                                                                                                               Commerce connects online and in-person payments for global retailers,
                                                                                                                               hospitality, and food & beverage groups. Platforms enables software providers to
                                                                                                                               embed payments and financial services, including capital, issuing, and business
                                                                                                                               accounts, into their offerings.
                                                                                                                               With this foundation, Adyen supports the full spectrum of how money moves for
                                                                                                                               the world’s largest enterprises and the fastest-growing software platforms
                                                                                                                               through a single, scalable solution.

   The Adyen Formula as a practical guide
   The Adyen Formula remains the foundation of how we operate. Unlike traditional
   value statements, it is practical and usable in day-to-day decision-making. It
   provides a shared set of working principles that guide teams through complex
   challenges and support consistency across regions. In many ways, it functions
   as a guide for how to succeed at Adyen: when in doubt, you can go back to the
   Formula and know what to do next. The Formula continues to guide teams
   across the company — not because we run programs around it, but because it
   works in practice.

   Diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI)
   Diversity of thoughts, backgrounds, and experiences has always strengthened
   our impact. Seeking out different perspectives to sharpen ideas is embedded in
   the Adyen Formula, and fostering an inclusive workplace where people can be
   their authentic selves remains central to how we operate. Strong internal
   communities, including our Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), play an important
   role in creating a sense of belonging and connection across the company.
   Our DEI efforts have increasingly focused on connection and impact beyond our
   walls, including ERG-led speaker series with external partners, allyship and
   growth programming, and inclusive office and event standards that support
   belonging in how we work every day.
   We apply these same principles not only to how we build our culture, but also to
   how we contribute to the communities around us. In 2025, we launched our
   Future Builders initiative, which increases access to technical education for

   At Adyen, we seek out different perspectives to
   sharpen our ideas. This is the cornerstone of my work
   in Financial Reporting: producing insightful and
   compliant financial statements requires translating the
   complexity of our global platform into clear, validated
   data for our stakeholders. It’s achieved by actively
   integrating input across different business pillars. By
   consolidating these diverse viewpoints, we ensure our
   financial reporting is technically sound, materially
   relevant, and delivers the genuine clarity that goes
   beyond compliance and earns stakeholder trust.
   Nosipho Nyathikazi
   Reporting Specialist

                                                                                                                               Financial objectives
                                                                                                                               Adyen's substantial long-term opportunity remains in
                                                                                                                               place, and we continue to build the business guided by
                                                                                                                               decisions that benefit us over that horizon. Our
                                                                                                                               financial objectives are:
                                                                                                                               Net revenue growth
                                                                                                                               We expect 2026 net revenue growth of 20 to 22% YoY on a constant currency
                                                                                                                               basis.

                                                                                                                               EBITDA margin
                                                                                                                               We expect to increase EBITDA margin levels to above 55% by 2028; we expect
                                                                                                                               2026 EBITDA margin to remain broadly in line with 2025.

                                                                                                                               Capital expenditure
                                                                                                                               We expect to maintain a sustainable capital expenditure level of up to 5% of our
                                                                                                                               net revenue.

                                                                                                                               Social impact
                                                                                                                               Our social impact work begins with people — individuals, nonprofit partners, and
                                                                                                                               local communities. We apply our time, skills, and resources where they have the
                                                                                                                               greatest effect, embedding these efforts into our day-to-day operations as a
                                                                                                                               global team.
                                                                                                                               In 2025, we continued to focus on four priority areas. In emergency response and
                                                                                                                               preparedness, we supported crisis-affected communities through matched
                                                                                                                               donations, volunteer time, and grants aimed at strengthening prevention and
                                                                                                                               resilience. In education, we expanded access to community learning with an
                                                                                                                               emphasis on digital and technology skills for under-served learners. Our
                                                                                                                               environmental sustainability efforts supported climate adaptation and innovation
                                                                                                                               aligned with Adyen’s footprint and ecosystem. And across local communities, our
                                                                                                                               offices identified regional priorities and acted on them through targeted funding
                                                                                                                               and hands-on volunteering.
                                                                                                                               Every colleague at Adyen receives paid time off to contribute to community
                                                                                                                               initiatives. This year, 43% of employees across all offices volunteered, up from 38%
                                                                                                                               last year, contributing a total of 12.6k hours. Our teams apply their expertise where
                                                                                                                               it could make a direct difference, supporting local nonprofits and participating in
                                                                                                                               community programs. These efforts are supported by our global network of
                                                                                                                               Community Impact Champions and funding from our 1% Commitment, as detailed
                                                                                                                               in the Social impact section of our Sustainability Statement.
                                                                                                                               Our structured grantmaking approach enables deeper, sustained engagement
                                                                                                                               with communities and nonprofit organizations. Catalytic grants combine financial
                                                                                                                               support with hands-on expertise across emergency response, education, and
                                                                                                                               environmental sustainability. Through strategic customer collaborations, we co-
                                                                                                                               create projects with customers and nonprofit partners where our priorities align.
                                                                                                                               As our strategy evolves, new avenues are emerging that extend support beyond
                                                                                                                               our immediate network, delivering resources to regions and organizations that
                                                                                                                               benefit most.
                                                                                                                               Across all of these efforts, our position at the intersection of payments,
                                                                                                                               technology, and global commerce allows us to reduce friction, solve complexity,
                                                                                                                               and enable impact at a scale that is difficult to replicate. Our role is not to
                                                                                                                               determine which issues matter most, but to enable our customers, partners, and
                                                                                                                               colleagues to make a meaningful difference using the full strength of our position
                                                                                                                               at the heart of global commerce.

                                                                                                                               our strategy and business objectives. We consider risk
                                                                                                                               as part of doing business and seek to be risk aware at
                                                                                                                               all times. Adyen applies a uniform and systematic
                                                                                                                               approach to risk management, based on the
                                                                                                                               Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework
                                                                                                                               issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations
                                                                                                                               of the Treadway Commission (COSO).

                                                                                                                               Risk governance
                                                                                                                               Adyen has established a risk governance structure that reflects the company’s
                                                                                                                               size, international footprint, complexity, and risk profile. This governance
                                                                                                                               framework sets out clear oversight responsibilities for risk management. The
                                                                                                                               Supervisory Board supervises and advises the Management Board. The Audit and
                                                                                                                               Risk Committee oversees, monitors, and advises the Management Board
                                                                                                                               regarding the functioning of the internal risk management and control systems.
                                                                                                                               The Management Board is responsible for maintaining an adequate system of risk
                                                                                                                               management and internal control. To support this, it has established a Risk
                                                                                                                               Committee. The Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Chief Risk and Compliance Officer
                                                                                                                               (CRCO), and Chief Technology Officer (CTO) represent the Management Board
                                                                                                                               in this committee, which also includes leaders of key risk-owning functions.
                                                                                                                               Adyen has organized its risk management according to risk types. The Enterprise
                                                                                                                               Risk function covers the financial, operational, technology, and strategic risks,
                                                                                                                               reporting its findings on the risk profile to the Risk Committee. The Internal
                                                                                                                               Control function maintains the internal control framework and reports on its
                                                                                                                               effectiveness to the Risk Committee.

   Operational cash management
   Operational cash management is fundamental to Adyen’s service offering and
   therefore central to our risk management framework. A payments platform must
   ensure a seamless flow of funds at all times — delivering payouts in the right
   amount, currency, and account, and at the right moment, in line with merchant
   preferences. Adyen supports this through sophisticated processes and a high
   degree of automation, which are essential to operating at scale.

                                                                                                                               External risk developments in 2025
                                                                                                                               In line with the previous year, concerns over global
                                                                                                                               trade policy, geopolitical tensions, and
                                                                                                                               macroeconomic uncertainty continued in 2025.
                                                                                                                               International trade policy – including the introduction
                                                                                                                               and increase of tariffs across sectors and trading
                                                                                                                               partners, followed by retaliatory measures – played a
                                                                                                                               significant role in the global political agenda and
                                                                                                                               economic environment. While Adyen delivered
                                                                                                                               resilient performance throughout the year, driven
                                                                                                                               primarily by net revenue expansion with existing
                                                                                                                               customers, our growth remains inherently linked to the
                                                                                                                               trajectories of our customers, many of whom
                                                                                                                               navigated an increasingly volatile environment. As a
                                                                                                                               result, Adyen’s net revenue growth was tempered by
                                                                                                                               tariff changes, which particularly impacted our largest
                                                                                                                               online retail merchants headquartered in APAC.
                                                                                                                               In the United States, policy uncertainty combined with geopolitical events and
                                                                                                                               rising concerns about a potential “AI bubble” contributed to elevated stock
                                                                                                                               market volatility. This also led to higher volatility in Adyen’s share price compared
                                                                                                                               to 2024. Although broader equity and commodity price volatility does not directly
                                                                                                                               affect Adyen’s financial results, the capital rebalancing seen early in the year,
                                                                                                                               primarily capital outflows from U.S. markets, contributed to a devaluation of the
                                                                                                                               U.S. dollar against the euro. This devaluation has persisted and negatively
                                                                                                                               impacted the translation of Adyen’s U.S. net revenues into euros.
                                                                                                                               While Adyen does not operate in countries affected by active armed conflict,
                                                                                                                               global geopolitical tensions significantly increased cybersecurity risks across

   Concentration of customers
   Large enterprise merchants typically work with multiple payment service                      Please refer to the Sustainability Statement for more detail on what
   providers to mitigate their own single-point-of-failure risk. As a result, these             Adyen considers material underlying risks to sustainability, and our
   customers may terminate contracts or shift volume elsewhere, which could                     methods of identification and mitigation of these risk types.
   reduce Adyen’s processed volumes and net revenue.
   Adyen has a low risk appetite for commercial dependency on individual
   customers. To mitigate this risk, the company continues to execute its growth
   strategy by onboarding new customers across diverse verticals. Adyen believes
   its merchant portfolio is well-diversified, supported by the breadth of payment
   channels available through the single platform. In the context of global
   macroeconomic uncertainty, this diversification helps reduce concentration risk.
   In recent years, Adyen’s growth has decreased the relative concentration of its
   largest merchants. However, onboarding new high-volume customers may
   temporarily increase concentration in the short term. Adyen monitors each
   merchant’s contribution to net revenue to inform commercial decisions and risk
   management. In 2025, global customer concentration remained within risk
   appetite. In certain regions, particularly those where Adyen has a newer
   presence, further diversification remains a core strategic priority.

   Sustainability risk
   Sustainability factors like environmental, climate, social and employee topics,
   human rights, and other societal developments can pose a risk to Adyen. These
   risks may materialize through impacts on our employees, operations, reputation,
   or the external stakeholders we work with.
   In recent years, regulatory requirements and stakeholder expectations related to
   sustainability have increased significantly, driving a global rise in data collection,
   public disclosure, and target-setting. Failing to keep pace with these
   developments, or failing to meet stated targets or expectations, could result in
   reputational harm or direct financial losses.

                                                                                                                               Financial risks
                                                                                                                               Adyen has a limited appetite to incur losses from
                                                                                                                               financial risks, please refer to Note 12 ‘Financial Risk
                                                                                                                               Management’ of the attached Consolidated Financial
                                                                                                                               Statements for additional disclosure.
                                                                                                                               Credit risk
                                                                                                                               Credit risk arises when a counterparty is unable to settle the full value of an
                                                                                                                               obligation when due or in accordance with agreed terms, resulting in a loss for
                                                                                                                               Adyen. It also includes a concentration dimension, referring to the risk of losses
                                                                                                                               from exposures clustered around a single counterparty or a connected group.
                                                                                                                               Adyen is primarily exposed to credit risk through cash and cash equivalents held
                                                                                                                               with commercial partner banks, receivables from card schemes and other
                                                                                                                               financial institutions, and pre-financing services provided to merchants. Adyen is
                                                                                                                               selective in choosing counterparties and actively monitors all resulting exposures.
                                                                                                                               Where partner banks are required to provide payment services in specific
                                                                                                                               situations, Adyen seeks to work with at least two different partners and, where
                                                                                                                               applicable, ensures that one of these is the regional central bank.
                                                                                                                               Throughout 2025, Adyen remained comfortably within its internally defined credit
                                                                                                                               risk and credit concentration limits, as well as the applicable regulatory thresholds.

                                                                                                                               Foreign exchange risk
                                                                                                                               Foreign exchange (FX) risk refers to the potential losses resulting from
                                                                                                                               fluctuations in FX rates against Adyen’s functional currency, the euro.
                                                                                                                               Movements in the euro affect the translation of Adyen’s foreign currency–
                                                                                                                               denominated net revenues as well as balance sheet positions. These balance
                                                                                                                               sheet exposures mainly relate to longer-term or perpetual items, such as foreign
                                                                                                                               currency cash balances, equity held to meet local liquidity or capital
                                                                                                                               requirements, contract assets, deferred tax assets, and accounts receivables and
                                                                                                                               payables. Adyen mitigates this risk through natural hedges and continuous
                                                                                                                               monitoring of its net open FX positions.
                                                                                                                               Adyen is additionally exposed to FX risk through commercial activity, most
                                                                                                                               notably in non-like-for-like acquiring transactions where the settlement FX rate

   Tax risk
   Adyen follows a conservative tax strategy underpinned by a low risk appetite
   where tax follows the business. We strive to be fully compliant with tax laws and
   regulations, upholding both the letter and the spirit of the law and paying the right
   amount of tax where value is created. We want to meet our obligations to
   stakeholders and the jurisdictions in which we operate. We prioritize sustainable
   and scalable practices that enable the business over tax planning.

   For more detail, we refer to our full Responsible Approach to Tax strategy
   published on our governance section online.

   As part of the 2025 double materiality assessment, responsible tax practices, as
   an element of broader business conduct, were identified as a material
   sustainability risk. Throughout 2025, the residual risk related to Adyen’s tax
   obligations remained within risk appetite.

   External reporting and disclosure risk
   Financial reporting, sustainability reporting, and regulatory reporting are integral
   components of Adyen’s risk management and internal control systems. Because
   each reporting obligation has its own requirements, the associated control
   systems and materiality thresholds differ. Adyen applies entity-specific
   materiality thresholds for financial reporting and has established dedicated
   internal controls for both sustainability and regulatory disclosures.
   Adyen has a low appetite for material errors and misstatements in financial and
   sustainability disclosures and reporting of regulatory ratios. A system of internal
   controls is in place to reduce the risk of error or loss and to provide reasonable
   assurance that financial records are reliable and prepared in accordance with
   applicable reporting standards. As with any system of internal control, these
   measures offer reasonable, though not absolute, assurance against material
   misstatement or loss. Furthermore internal controls are in place to ensure limited
   assurance on sustainability disclosures.
   Throughout the year, Adyen’s first- and second-line teams systematically
   evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls, actively adapting and
   strengthening them in response to changing environments and emerging risks.

                                                                                                                               Integrity risk
                                                                                                                               As a regulated financial institution, Adyen plays a key
                                                                                                                               role as a gatekeeper to the international financial
                                                                                                                               system and is entrusted with protecting the integrity of
                                                                                                                               financial markets. In line with our commitment to
                                                                                                                               building an ethical business, Adyen prioritizes and
                                                                                                                               maintains the highest standards of integrity in
                                                                                                                               everything we do.
                                                                                                                               Effectively managing integrity risks at scale remained a key priority in 2025.
                                                                                                                               Guided by the principles of the Global Integrity Strategy, Adyen continued to
                                                                                                                               identify, monitor, and mitigate integrity risks through a comprehensive framework
                                                                                                                               of global standards. These standards cover a broad range of risk areas, including
                                                                                                                               bribery and corruption, conflicts of interest, socially unacceptable behavior,
                                                                                                                               market abuse, data privacy, fraud, money laundering, terrorism financing,
                                                                                                                               sanctions violations, and proliferation financing.
                                                                                                                               This framework ensures that integrity risks, together with the diverse laws and
                                                                                                                               regulations governing Adyen’s global operations, are addressed consistently and
                                                                                                                               effectively, while supporting scalable risk management. By embedding global
                                                                                                                               integrity standards into the core of its technology stack, Adyen reinforces its
                                                                                                                               commitment to solving challenges through innovation and maintaining the trust of
                                                                                                                               its stakeholders.
                                                                                                                               Integrity risk includes compliance risk factors as referred to in the 2025 Dutch
                                                                                                                               Corporate Governance Code and the Statement by the Management Board.
                                                                                                                               Further detail on how Adyen manages specific integrity risks can be found in the
                                                                                                                               subsections that follow, as well as in the Sustainability Statement for topics such
                                                                                                                               as financial crime and data privacy.

                                                                                                                               Fraud risk
                                                                                                                               Adyen recognizes that fraud risks, particularly external fraud attempts, will
                                                                                                                               always be present. To manage this, Adyen sets clear limits on the acceptance of
                                                                                                                               prospective customers or third parties based on fraud-related risk factors, such as

                                                                 Adyen works diligently to comply with the Code, though we apply a stricter
                                                                 standard regarding board appointments and dismissals. While Best Practice
                                                                 provision 4.3.3 of the Code allows shareholders to cancel a binding nomination or
                                                                 dismiss a board member with a one-third majority of issued capital, Adyen
                                                                 requires a one-half majority. This higher threshold stems from a previous
                                                                 shareholder agreement and supports our focus on long-term stability.


                                                                 General meeting, shares, and shareholders
                                                                 General Meeting
                                                                 Adyen holds an annual general meeting (AGM) before the end of June. Additional
                                                                 general meetings may be convened when the Management Board or the
                                                                 Supervisory Board considers this necessary.
                                                                 For each share, shareholders may cast one vote in the AGM. Resolutions are
                                                                 passed by an absolute majority of votes cast, unless otherwise outlined in
                                                                 Adyen’s Articles of Association. Votes can be cast at the AGM either in person or
                                                                 by proxy.
                                                                 In 2025, Adyen continued to offer Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) that convert into
                                                                 shares. Please refer to Note 4.3 in the Consolidated Financial Statements for
                                                                 further information.

   Diversity, equity, and inclusion at Adyen
   The Supervisory Board aims for a balance in its composition with respect to
   gender, nationality, age, experience, and affinity with the nature and culture of the
   business of Adyen in all countries in which it is active. The Supervisory Board
   values and promotes diversity, both within the Supervisory Board and the
   Management Board, as within Adyen in general. Differences in educational
   background, nationality, age, race, gender, experiences, and beliefs, among
   others, are vital to the business, enabling the Boards and the company to look at
   issues and opportunities differently and to respond to challenges in new ways.
   Diversity, equity and inclusion are key drivers for innovation and allows Adyen to
   attract and retain top talent.
   The Supervisory Board has drawn up the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Policy,
   which has been established in accordance with Best Practice Provision 2.1.5. of
   the Code. The Adyen Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Policy can be found at our
   Governance webpage via investors.adyen.com/governance. For more
   information on this policy, the related actions and commitments, please refer to
   the Sustainability Statement on page 123.


   Appreciation
   Looking back at 2025, the Supervisory Board would like to thank all Adyen
   employees for their contribution during the past year. We are proud to see the
   team continue building long-term value for customers and other stakeholders,

   Service and severance agreements
   All Management Board members have entered into a service agreement
   (overeenkomst van opdracht) with Adyen N.V. The terms and conditions of these
   service agreements have been aligned with applicable laws and regulations and
   the Dutch Corporate Governance Code. The remuneration in the event of
   dismissal does not exceed one year’s salary (the “fixed” remuneration
   component). In the financial year 2025, no severance payment has been paid to
   any Management Board member.

   Loans
   No loans, advance payments, and guarantees have been granted to or on behalf
   of the Management Board members.

   Risk management and internal controls over
   sustainability reporting
   The Sustainability Statement, including all relevant data points, is prepared by the
   ESG reporting team, which sits in Adyen’s Group Finance function. This report is
   written with support from subject matter experts across the business. Within
   sustainability reporting, Adyen identifies the key risk of using incomplete or
   inaccurate data.
   In order to identify and manage risks associated with sustainability reporting, we
   have implemented several measures, including:
   Risk assessments: Please refer to the Risk management section on Event
   identification and risk assessment. During these risk assessments, we identify and
   evaluate key risks, including those which could impact the quality of Adyen’s
   sustainability reporting and our ability to comply with ESG reporting standards.
   Systems: Sustainability information is collected from several functions within our
   organization. Our current processes are a mix of data management platforms and
   manual processes. We are continuously exploring solutions that will further
   enhance our data collection, efficiency, and quality.
   Internal controls: Adyen’s Internal Control team works with stakeholders to
   ensure effective controls and that coverage is in place to manage sustainability
   reporting-related risks. Sustainability reporting controls have been part of Adyen’s
   Internal Control System (ICS) since 2023 and continue to be matured taking into
   account the latest results from risk assessment (e.g. DMA) and control testing.
   Internal reporting: Developments related to sustainability reporting risks and
   findings resulting from evaluation of the ESG controls framework are shared with
   the Supervisory Board, Management Board and the Risk Committee on an
   ongoing basis.

                                                                 Understanding our stakeholders and integrating their
                                                                 views and feedback
                                                                 To ensure this holistic approach, we continuously engage with the groups most
                                                                 critical to our business and those most impacted by our operations. Consistent with
                                                                 our 2024 assessment, our key stakeholders include employees, our customers,
                                                                 shareholders, suppliers, regulators, nonprofit partners, and society at large.
                                                                 We use diverse and frequent modes of engagement with stakeholders to ensure
                                                                 clear feedback and act quickly on their concerns and expectations. Below is a
                                                                 summary of Adyen’s key stakeholders, the ways we engage with them, and the
                                                                 primary themes of engagement.
                                                                 The outcomes of these engagements are reviewed by our leadership teams and
                                                                 Management Board. They are taken into consideration during strategic
                                                                 discussions to refine Adyen’s operational practices and sustainability approach
                                                                 where deemed necessary. The way the stakeholder views are shared with
                                                                 leadership differs depending on the stakeholder group and the frequency and
                                                                 format of engagement. For example, views from employees are shared annually
                                                                 as part of our culture and inclusion (C&I) survey results, whereas the views from
                                                                 customers are reviewed on an ad hoc basis to align with our leadership’s different
                                                                 touchpoints with customers throughout the year.


                                                                 Integration of stakeholder views
                                                                 Stakeholder feedback is integrated into decision-making through two
                                                                 complementary processes. First, our ongoing engagement activities enable us to
                                                                 gather continuous input and act quickly on concerns or expectations as they arise.
                                                                 Second, the DMA process provides a structured and periodic assessment that
                                                                 consolidates a wide set of stakeholder perspectives and validates them against

   Outcome of the 2025 DMA review
   The 2025 DMA review confirmed the continued relevance of the material topics
   identified in 2024, while iterating and improving the granularity of underlying IRO
   definitions. The assessment focused on refining existing topics to ensure closer
   alignment with Adyen’s business model, governance structure and sustainability
   priorities, while further aligning topic definitions with ESRS requirements, for
   instance, the refinement of the Data privacy and data protection topic.
   Building on the foundation of the 2024 DMA, the 2025 review led to a number of
   targeted updates:
   ▪ Ways of working (formerly Company culture): Refined to emphasize the
     elements of company culture that drive the most material opportunities and
     long-term success for Adyen.
   ▪ People growth (formerly Learning & development): Refined to better reflect
     the empowerment of employees to take ownership of their growth and
     development, maintaining a focus on both opportunity and impact.
   ▪ Data privacy and data protection: Relevant Information security aspects
     related to data protection have been consolidated under this newly defined
     topic, and the associated risk has been refined accordingly.
   ▪ Business conduct: Further broken down into distinct sub-risks to provide more
     granular insights and a clearer view of each risk area for reporting purposes.

   Our business resilience
   Integrating sustainability matters into our strategy and decision-making is
   fundamental to our business resilience. By strengthening diversity, upholding
   strong ethical business practices, and reducing our environmental footprint, we
   mitigate material risks and ensure the long-term viability of our business model.
   While we do not yet have a complete view of the current and expected financial
   effects of our material sustainability risks and opportunities, we are continuously
   embedding the implications of new directives and regulations into our strategy
   and business model. We consider our strategy and business model to be resilient
   and well-equipped to manage the aforementioned identified risks while
   maximising our opportunities, ensuring sustainable growth over the long term. We
   perform resilience analysis in the form of stress testing as outlined further in the
   Risk management section.
   Our 2025 targeted review of the DMA, conducted in alignment with ESRS,
   confirmed the ongoing relevance of the sustainability matters identified in 2024.
   No new material topics were identified; instead, the review focused on refining
   existing topics for greater clarity. As a result, we have maintained our strategic
   focus and initiatives without requiring significant changes to our business model
   or operations. This consistency reflects a stable and well-understood landscape
   of sustainability-related risks and opportunities.
   We have aligned the disclosure of our sustainability matters with the
   requirements of the ESRS. Besides ESRS-related sustainability matters, we also
   report on entity-specific sustainability matters. While not explicitly covered by the
   ESRS, these are part of our license to operate and critical to our long-term
   sustainability performance. Please refer to the following section for an overview
   of the disclosure requirements covered in our Sustainability Statement.

   offices, up from 13 in 2024. This improved granularity enabled us to verify that our
   major EMEA offices operate on renewable energy, a confirmation that was not
   previously possible. Creating this scalable process is an important step on our
   path toward achieving 100% renewable energy for our Scope 2 emissions by
   2030. This ongoing improvement effort is global in scope and will continue to be
   rolled out with a prioritized focus on our top 10 largest offices and locations where
   we have higher operational control.

   Evaluating our suppliers’ sustainability journey (Scope 3)
   In 2024, we conducted an initial supplier survey with our hardware partners to
   establish a baseline understanding of their sustainability maturity. A key insight
   from this baseline was the need to formalize our sustainability expectations
   across our value chain. Building on this learning, our focus in 2025 shifted towards
   broader engagement and expanded to include all strategic partners. We launched
   an initiative to drive the adoption of our updated Supplier Code of Conduct
   (SCoC) across these partners. To ensure effectiveness, we integrated this
   objective into our procurement function by setting internal targets for
   procurement managers to secure SCoC adherence. Additionally, we expanded
   our data engagement by formally requesting GHG accounting capabilities and
   LCA data from key hardware partners. While we have not yet modelled specific
   carbon reductions from these actions, embedding sustainability requirements into
   procurement negotiations has established the governance needed to drive
   reductions going forward.

   For both physical and transition risk scenarios, our methodology followed a three-
   step process: first, identifying relevant risk scenarios; second, linking scenario
   impacts to financial risk categories; and third, quantifying potential exposure and
   losses. The chosen scenarios represent the full range of plausible physical and
   transition risks for our business model. Both scenarios incorporated
   macroeconomic variables such as GDP growth, exchange rates, and policy
   interest rates to evaluate potential impacts on Adyen’s business model. The
   qualitative findings demonstrate high resilience: under the high-transition risk
   scenario, the impact on net income before taxes is projected not to exceed 2%
   over the long term. Conversely, this scenario highlighted a potential financial
   opportunity where projected rises in global interest rates could increase our net
   financial income. Under the high-physical risk scenario “Current Policies,” the
   maximum modelled impact on net income was a decrease of less than 3.5%. Our
   climate analysis is compatible with our financial statements due to it being based
   on our 10-year forecast model at a consolidated level.

   EU Taxonomy report                                                                      Statement on Taxonomy alignment
                                                                                           In accordance with the derogation provided for in the Commissions Delegated
   Regulatory background and scope                                                         Regulation of July 2025, Adyen states the following for the Financial Year 2025:
   As a credit institution, Adyen has an obligation to disclose information referred to
                                                                                           No activities are claimed as being associated with economic activities that
   in Article 8(1) of Regulation (EU) 2020/852 (the “Taxonomy Regulation”). The
                                                                                           qualify as environmentally sustainable under Articles 3 and 9 of Regulation
   EU Taxonomy was introduced to provide a common classification system for
                                                                                           (EU) 2020/852 (Taxonomy Regulation).
   sustainable economic activities in support of the Action Plan on Financing
   Sustainable Growth.
                                                                                           Future reporting strategy
   On January 5, 2026, the European Commission adopted a Delegated Regulation
   (EU) 2026/73 amending the Taxonomy Disclosures Delegated Act to streamline              This application of the simplification measures represents a temporary deferral of
   and simplify reporting obligations. A key component of this simplification package      detailed quantitative reporting, not a permanent withdrawal from ESG
   is the introduction of a temporary relief for financial undertakings, allowing them     transparency.
   to defer the reporting of detailed quantitative Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)       Adyen anticipates resuming detailed EU Taxonomy reporting for the Financial
   until 31 December 2027, provided a specific statement regarding alignment is            Year 2027 (reporting year 2028). This timeline aligns with the expiration of the
   included in the management report.                                                      temporary relief and entry into force of the postponed reporting requirements for
                                                                                           the KPI on Fees and Commissions Income. Adyen will continue to actively
   Application of simplification measures (Opt-Out)                                        monitor regulatory developments and enhance its data infrastructure to ensure a
                                                                                           smooth transition to mandatory reporting for the Financial Year 2027.
   Adyen has elected to utilize the temporary relief option for the Financial Year
   2025. This decision is driven by the limited relevance of the standard credit
   institution KPIs - specifically the Green Asset Ratio (GAR) - to Adyen’s specific
   business model.
   As detailed in previous Annual Reports, Adyen’s core business model is not that
   of traditional lending or financing, but rather generating revenue from payment
   processing and settlement fees. Consequently, Adyen’s assets are primarily
   short-term in nature. In the 2024 Annual Report, Adyen reported a Green Asset
   Ratio (GAR) between 0.08% and 0.2%, confirming this metric is not a material
   driver for Adyen nor a meaningful indicator of the company’s contribution to a
   sustainable economy.
   By utilizing this relief, Adyen directs its resources toward preparing for the future
   mandatory reporting of the Fees and Commissions KPI, which is considered a
   more relevant indicator for its transaction-based business model.

   What I love most about working at Adyen is that no
   two days are the same. Working in recruitment, you're
   constantly tackling challenges that are new and
   unique, which is why the formula point 'We seek out
   different perspectives to sharpen our ideas' is truly at
   the heart of what I do every day.

   We're so proud of our diverse, international culture
   here. It's not just a nice thing to have; it's a massive
   advantage. When we bring together a wide range of
   different mindsets to look at a challenge, it
   consistently surfaces creative solutions I never would
   have thought of on my own.
   Lachlan Diver
   Recruitment Business Partner

                                                                                                                               Actions
                                                                                                                               In 2025, we took the following key actions to strengthen our anti-financial crime
                                                                                                                               framework, effectively address associated financial crime risks, and continue
                                                                                                                               meeting our policy objectives.

                                                                                                                               Our Systematic Integrity Risk Analysis (‘SIRA’)
                                                                                                                               SIRA ensures that Adyen continues to proactively identify and effectively mitigate
                                                                                                                               integrity risks that may affect our business — including accounting for evolution
                                                                                                                               within our product offering, the markets in which Adyen operates, and our general
                                                                                                                               growth as a business . By serving as a steering mechanism for the Management
                                                                                                                               Board, the SIRA ensures that Adyen’s Control Framework remains robust and fit-
                                                                                                                               for-purpose to address the integrity risks to which Adyen may be exposed.
                                                                                                                               Recognizing the importance of this process, Adyen has continued to enhance its
                                                                                                                               SIRA in accordance with the latest integrity risk assessment guidance and
                                                                                                                               standards to which it is subject. Examples of such improvements have included
                                                                                                                               the identification, incorporation, and analysis of new integrity risks, continued
                                                                                                                               maturation of our risk assessment methodology, and strengthened oversight of
                                                                                                                               risk analysis results and corresponding follow up actions with which to ensure the
                                                                                                                               sustained strength and effectiveness of the Adyen Control Framework.
                                                                                                                               On an ongoing basis, Adyen also performs transaction filtering and monitoring
                                                                                                                               and periodic or event-driven reviews of customers. We also, where necessary,
                                                                                                                               terminate business relationships that are beyond our risk appetite.
                                                                                                                               These actions apply to all regions where Adyen operates, across all areas of our
                                                                                                                               operations, and to all members of our workforce.

                                                                                                                               Looking ahead
                                                                                                                               Looking ahead, Adyen will continue to prioritize and strengthen our anti-financial
                                                                                                                               crime framework. This includes ongoing enhancements to our transaction
                                                                                                                               monitoring systems and the continuous refinement of our internal processes,
                                                                                                                               ensuring that our measures remain both effective and efficient. By streamlining
                                                                                                                               workflows, we safeguard our ability to act swiftly and decisively in mitigating
                                                                                                                               financial crime.
                                                                                                                               We remain committed to investing in both our people and our technology.
                                                                                                                               Through ongoing employee training and the use of advanced tools, such as

    Net interest revenue


        Accounting policy – Net interest income
        Adyen presents net interest income as part of net revenue, as it is earned through the Company's revenue
        generating activities, and includes financial instruments measured using the effective interest method.
        Interest income and expenses on financial instruments are recognised in the income statement on an accrual
        basis using the effective interest rate method.
        The effective interest rate calculation method includes estimated future cash flows determined by all of the
        contractual terms of the asset or liability, such as interest, amortisation of any discount or premium or other
        differences, including transaction costs and qualifying fees and commissions, over the expected lives of the
        assets and liabilities. The effective interest rate is the rate that exactly discounts estimated future cash flows
        to the net carrying amount of the asset. As a result, this method requires Adyen to estimate future cash flows,
        in some cases based on its experience with client behaviour, considering all contractual terms of the financial
        instrument, as well as the expected lives of the assets and liabilities.



   Adyen's financial product offering includes Accounts, in the form of merchant-related funds held in business accounts, and
   Capital, in the form of loans and advances. Adyen earns interest income on funds held in Accounts, Capital loans and
   advances issued, and the sale of terminals with a financing agreement. Simultaneously, Adyen incurs interest expense
   related to the deposited funds held in the Accounts. During 2025, Adyen earned net interest income of EUR 12,573 (2024:
   EUR 8,299), which mainly relates to the Accounts product offering.
   Interest earned on cash balances outside of aforementioned products, are not classified within net interest income but
   form part of net finance income. Refer to note 10 'Cash and cash equivalents '.
