   3. Inventories
   Inventories relate to the point of sale (POS) terminals in connection with the roll out of the Unified Commerce strategy.



         Accounting policy – Inventories
         Inventories are measured at the lower of cost or net realizable value. The cost of inventories is based on the
         first-in, first-out method (FIFO) and includes expenditure incurred in acquiring the inventories and other costs
         incurred in bringing them to their existing location and condition. Net realizable value is defined by Adyen as
         the estimated re-sell price in the ordinary course of business.
         The carrying amount of inventories is recognized as an expense when the inventories are sold or written off,
         unless they form part of the cost of another asset.

        Accounting policy – Functional currency and foreign currency translation                                                 Adyen has classified the convertible preferred Visa Inc. shares as a financial instrument at fair value through profit or loss.
                                                                                                                                 For 2025, the effect on other financial results is a net gain of EUR 184 (2024: EUR 3,490 ) relating to an exchange loss of
        The functional currency of Adyen N.V. is the Euro as the Euro area is the primary economic environment in
                                                                                                                                 EUR (1,162) (2024: EUR 424 exchange gain) and fair value gain of EUR 1,346 (2024: EUR 3,066). Refer to note 11 ‘Financial
        which Adyen operates. The financial statements of entities that have a functional currency different from
                                                                                                                                 instruments’ for more detail on the other financial assets at FVPL.
        Adyen N.V. (“foreign operations”) are translated into Euros as follows:
        ▪ Assets, equity and liabilities – at the closing rate at the date of the statement of financial position;
        ▪ Income and expenses – at the average rate of the period (as this is considered a reasonable approximation
          of the actual rates prevailing at the transaction dates).
        Foreign currency differences are recognized in other comprehensive income and are presented within equity
        in the legal reserves.
        Monetary items
        Monetary items are units of currency held and assets and liabilities to be received or paid in a fixed or
        determinable number of units of currency. Monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies
        are retranslated into Adyen’s functional currency at the rates prevailing on the balance sheet date. Exchange
        rate differences resulting from the settlement of such transactions and from the translation at year-end
        exchange rates of monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are recognized in the
        statement of comprehensive income within “other financial results”.

        Non-monetary items
        Non-monetary items that are measured in terms of historical cost in a foreign currency are translated using
        the exchange rate at the date of the transaction. Non-monetary assets and liabilities that are measured at fair
        value through profit or loss are retranslated at the date that the fair value is determined.

        Accounting estimate – Deferred tax assets linked to windfall benefits
        Windfall benefits arise when the tax deduction for share-based compensation exceeds the cumulative
        remuneration expense recognized for accounting purposes. Deferred tax assets include tax losses carried
        forward relating to options exercised in the United States at a Federal and State level (December 31, 2025:
        EUR 56,174; December 31, 2024: EUR 80,364) and windfall benefits relating to options granted and vested,
        however not yet exercised (December 31, 2025: EUR 1,581; December 31, 2024: 2,662). An amount of EUR
        14,507 of the tax losses carried forward was utilised during the period and recognised in the share premium
        reserve (2024: EUR 16,840).

        During 2025, Adyen has reassessed the recoverability of deferred tax assets on windfall benefits linked to
        the share-based compensation plan in the United States. Adyen continues to recognize deferred tax assets
        that will be realized against future profits on a going concern basis.

        The United States Federal Tax windfall benefit continues to be recognized as these carry forward losses on a
        Federal level have no expiration date. The State net operating losses continues to be recognized as these
        carry forward losses are expected to be utilized against future taxable income before its expiration date.
        This windfall benefit has been recognized assuming all options granted to date will be exercised within the
        8th anniversary of the grant date (grant date + 7 years).

   Other financial assets at FVPL
   Adyen has recognized and classified the convertible (‘Series C’) preferred Visa Inc. shares within the FVPL category. The fair
   value of the level 2 preferred shares in Visa Inc. is based on the quoted price of Visa Inc. common shares, adjusted for lack of
   marketability, multiplied by an initial conversion rate of preferred shares into common shares. The conversion rate may be
   updated in the future. The adjustment for lack of marketability is determined using an option pricing model technique which
   relies on observable market data of the underlying Visa Inc. common shares, as well as a presumed length of holding period
   restriction on the preferred shares.
   A partial conversion of the Series C preferred stock into Series A preferred stock took place during 2025. The Series A
   preferred stock were converted into Visa Inc. common stock and sold prior to the end of 2025 at fair market value.

   12.          Financial risk management
   Adyen’s activities generally produce a variety of financial risks. Risk management is the responsibility of Adyen’s management. Adyen applies a risk-aware but not unduly risk-averse approach toward risk management. Adyen’s Integral Risk
   Management Framework (IRMF), which is based on COSO’s Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) model, defines a uniform and systematic approach for managing risks across Adyen. The main sources of financial risk to Adyen are considered in the
   table below:
    SOURCE OF RISK AND RISK DESCRIPTION            RISK MITIGATION                                                                                                                                                     REMAINING RISK
    Liquidity risk                                                                                                                                                                                                     Minimal

    Liquidity risk is the risk that Adyen is not   As a result of its business model, the majority of Adyen’s liquidity needs are short-term in nature. In the default set-up Adyen follows a ‘pass-through’           Adyen’s balance sheet is by nature short-

    Interest rate risk is defined as the risk   Adyen’s business model is primarily fee-based while interest income does not constitute a key revenue component of the client-facing product offering.                      Adyen accepts the interest rate risk
    that changes in interest rates lead to an   Despite the fee-based business model, Adyen’s balance sheet has various characteristics that are relevant from an interest rate risk perspective. 1) Adyen’s                stemming from its cash position as part of

                                                     •     Changes in interest rates directly translate into the price of assets but not into the price of liabilities. This impacts primarily net finance income, and to
                                                           a lesser extent, interest income (as part of net revenues). Accordingly, the portfolio is sensitive to downward interest rate movements. The total
                                                           income sensitivity for material currencies (EUR, USD, GBP, BRL and AUD) to a plausible parallel interest rate move up and down (+/-50bps for
                                                           EUR, USD, GBP and AUD and +/-100bps for BRL) amounts to about EUR +/-47 million, respectively. Adyen calculates this sensitivity on a constant
                                                           balance sheet assumption and a 1Y projection horizon. The contribution of client-facing commercial products (e.g. Adyen Capital or Terminal
                                                           Finance) to this sensitivity is only 0.19% (or EUR 90k) and, thus, immaterial.

                                                     •     There is only limited value sensitivity to interest rate movements due to the fact that both assets and liabilities are on average very short-dated. The
                                                           total economic value sensitivity for material currencies to the same plausible parallel interest rate move up and down, amounts to EUR +/-3.2
                                                           million, respectively. The economic value sensitivity is calculated on a run-off balance sheet assumption. The contribution of client-facing
                                                           commercial products is EUR +/- 84k and, thus, immaterial.

                                                   Receivables from merchants:
                                                   As part of the accelerated Sales Day Payout product, Adyen settles a full sales day of transactions to merchants before the funds from financial institutions
                                                   are fully received. The receivable is effectively secured through the authorization and capture of a transaction, leading to a commitment to pay by the card
                                                   schemes. As a result of the nature of the payment transactions the duration of the accelerated Sales Day Payout balances is very short (average duration
                                                   between 2-3 days). Adyen assesses, on a forward-looking basis, the expected credit losses. The impact of credit losses on receivables from merchants is
                                                   expected to be insignificant. Balances of merchant-facing Capital loans and cash advances remain insignificant.

                                                   Other financial assets:
                                                   The remaining financial asset credit risk exposure (such as trade and other receivables and Brazil government bonds ) is considered to be limited. Adyen
                                                   manages its credit risk through robust underwriting, ongoing monitoring, and timely collection efforts to manage potential defaults effectively. During 2025,

   18.          Other contingent assets, liabilities and commitments


            Accounting policy - Contingent assets, liabilities and other commitments


            Contingent liabilities consist of possible obligations, whose existence will be confirmed by uncertain future
            events, and present obligations where the transfer of economic resources is uncertain or cannot be reliably
            measured.
            Adyen discloses contingent liabilities if the likelihood of an outflow of economic resources is not probable or
            if the likelihood of an outflow of economic resources is more likely than not, but the amount cannot be
            reliably measured.

            Contingent assets are possible assets whose existence will be confirmed by uncertain future events.
            Adyen discloses contingent assets where an inflow of economic benefits is probable.




   Adyen N.V. and Adyen International B.V. are a fiscal unity for corporate income tax purposes. The members of the fiscal
   unity are jointly and severally liable for any taxes payable by the fiscal unity.

   Adyen has EUR 109,411 of outstanding bank guarantees and letters of credit as at December 31, 2025 (2024: EUR 138,430).

                                                                                                                                   Reporting methodology
   24.      Tax Transparency                                                                                                       Data is primarily derived from standalone IFRS financial records, aggregated by jurisdiction in line with the EU Public CbCR
                                                                                                                                   Directive. To accurately reflect our operational intensity, we voluntarily also include Operating Expenses. This has been
   Responsible tax management is integral to our long-term sustainable growth. We’re committed to pay taxes where business
                                                                                                                                   done on a consolidated basis, removing the effect of internal transactions to show the true cost of our local footprint.
   is conducted and value is created. Adyen is headquartered in the Netherlands and is subject to corporate income tax in all
   jurisdictions where it has a taxable presence. Our centralized operating model aligns with our integrated global business
   model and financial technology infrastructure. We apply Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development                  Defining our contribution
   (OECD)-compliant transfer pricing methodologies to ensure local entities and offices are compensated on an arm’s length         We categorize our tax footprint into two distinct groups:
   basis for their contributions to the group’s business. Consequently, the majority of the group's profit and related income
   taxes are recognized in the Netherlands, reflecting the substance of our Dutch headquarter activities.                               •    Mandatory CbCR Metrics*: prepared in strict accordance with the EU Public CbCR Directive, covering FTE,
                                                                                                                                             (Gross) Revenue (including intercompany), Profit (Loss) Before Income Tax, Income Tax Accrued (Current Year),
   We view tax as a critical component of our broader ESG commitment and our overall contribution to the jurisdictions where                 Accumulated Earnings and Income Taxes Paid.
   we operate. Our Total Tax Contribution (TTC) quantifies our financial impact through Taxes Borne, which represent a direct
   cost to our business, and Taxes Collected, which we administer and remit on behalf of governments and third parties.                 •    Voluntary Economic Metrics*: these capture our broader financial reality, including Operating Expenses, Income
                                                                                                                                             Tax Expense, Taxes Collected (Indirect Taxes, Payroll Taxes, Withholding Taxes remitted) and Grants /
   The Management Board, through its Co-CEOs, CFO and other board members, ensures due observance of the five tax                            Incentives received.
   pillars set forth in our 'Responsible Approach to Tax'. Adyen utilizes a tax control framework to identify, assess and manage
   global tax risks in a manner consistent with our low risk appetite. As a financial technology company, we leverage our core     We believe transparency requires showing our actual tax footprint. By subtracting government support from our total tax
   capabilities to build advanced, automated tax processes. This not only enhances efficiency, but also minimizes human error,     payments, we provide a 'net' view of our financial relationship with each country.
   ensuring larger levels of accuracy and compliance, resulting in a higher level of control.

   24.4.     Innovation Box
   Adyen builds a global financial technology platform capable of meeting the rapidly evolving needs of fast-growing global
   businesses. Continuous innovation and technology are critical to meet the changing payment and fintech industry dynamics
   and the needs of our merchants. Governments worldwide facilitate innovative R&D activities through Grants and Incentives.
   One of the facilities offered by the Dutch government is the Dutch Innovation Box. Following the application of the
   innovation box, profits attributable to qualifying innovations are taxed at a Dutch corporate income tax rate of 9%, opposed
   to the corporate income tax rate of 25.8%. As Adyen strives to continuously innovate its global financial technology
   platform, Adyen applies the innovation box to reinvest those benefits in the further development of the platform and growth
   of the company.
   Adyen concluded an agreement with the Dutch tax authorities to obtain upfront certainty on the percentage of taxable profit
   that qualifies for the innovation box. Based on this agreement the percentage of taxable profit of Adyen N.V. qualifying for
   the innovation box is directly linked with the number of hours spent by developers on R&D projects (WBSO).

   24.5.     Transfer Pricing
   We apply OECD-compliant transfer pricing methodologies to ensure that our head office and local offices are compensated
   on an arm’s length basis for their contributions to the group’s business. Transfer pricing involves significant judgment and
   estimation, which may be subject to challenge by tax authorities. Adyen maintains contemporaneous documentation in
   accordance with local regulations and the OECD Guidelines and, where appropriate, seeks upfront certainty through
   (bilateral) Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) with local tax authorities to ensure intercompany transactions reflect
   economic reality and the 'arm's length' principle.


   24.6.     Global Minimum Taxation - Pillar Two
   The OECD Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) introduced the Pillar Two model rules to address
   tax challenges arising from the digitalization of the global economy. This international framework establishes a global
   minimum tax standard, ensuring that the worldwide profits of multinational groups are subject to an ETR of at least 15% in
   every jurisdiction where they operate.
   Adyen N.V. is within the scope of the OECD Pillar Two model rules. Under this legislation, Adyen is liable for a top-up tax for
   the difference between the Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) ETR per jurisdiction and the 15% minimum rate. This has no
   material impact on Adyen N.V. in 2025.

        Accounting policy – Leases
        Adyen assesses if a lease exists or a contract contains a lease at the contract inception date, concluding                      Additions                                                                          50,780        33,484
        whether an asset is identifiable, and Adyen has control to direct its use and all related economic benefits. A                  Depreciation for the period                                                       (40,655)      (33,915)
        right-of-use asset and a lease liability are recognized at the lease commencement date, which can differ from
                                                                                                                                        Other movements                                                                    (3,222)         1,201
        contract inception date.
        The lease liability is initially measured by bringing to present value all future lease payments, discounted by                 Balance - December 31                                                             175,520       168,617
        an incremental borrowing rate, in case no interest rate is available for the contract.
        At initial recognition, the right of use asset amounts to the initial lease liability. Right of use assets are tested           Recognized right-of-use asset                                                     318,403       276,438
        for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicates that the carrying amount may not be
                                                                                                                                        Accumulated depreciation                                                         (142,884)      (107,821)
        recoverable.
        Short-term (less than 12 months) and small value lease contracts are expensed in statement of                                   Balance - December 31                                                             175,520       168,617
        comprehensive income on a straight-line basis over the lease term.

   Other information
   Provisions in the Articles of Association relating to profit appropriation
   Article 34 of the Articles of Association of Adyen provide that the appropriation of the net income for the year is decided
   upon at the General Meeting.
   For the preferred dividends the General Meeting can elect to pay out the annual dividend on these shares or to add the
   dividend to the class reserve.
